Current focus: club path. Trackman (14 Nov) confirmed an out-to-in path on every club (7-iron −5°, 2-iron −6°). Compression is already good, so it's off the list. Everything this block is built to move your 7-iron path from −5° towards −2°.

Four pillars

1 · Long game — Wednesdays. Path drills on the 7-iron, sweep the 2-iron, face control with the driver.

2 · Home — 10 minutes, 4–5 days a week. Chair drill, slow pump reps, finish holds, putting mat.

3 · Short game & putting — every second weekend. Open-face wedge work, distance ladders, the putting rebuild.

4 · Play — log real rounds here; the goals and caddy's read show if the range work is transferring.

The weekly rhythm

Wed ~80 balls — Trackman bay. Score only the transfer shots.

Home, most days — 10–13 minutes, no ball needed.

Alt. weekend ~1.5hr — short game, chipping green, bunkers, putting.

Two rules. One swing thought per ball, never two. And hold every full-swing finish for 3 seconds; if you fall back, that shot doesn't count.

When to bring data back to the chat

Every 2–3 Wednesdays — Trackman PDF export (columns in the Trackman tab) plus Practice → Log → Copy log.

Every 4–5 rounds — Rounds → Send to Claude.

2 iron vs 5 wood off the tee

2 iron — tight holes, into/cross wind, firm running fairways. Low and penetrating. While the path is being fixed, check your tee-shot data in the app before treating it as the safe option.

5 wood — max carry, soft conditions, long par 3s needing a soft landing, calm days where distance wins.

Trackman targets

Driver — spin 2,200–2,600 rpm · launch 12–14° · smash > 1.45.

5 wood / 2 iron — watch attack angle: shallow sweep, not a steep chop.

7 iron — chase a tight carry spread; target 88–92 mph to load the Project X IO shaft.

Adding a course with hole maps

Step-by-step guide
  1. Check it's mapped. Search the course on openyardage.com. If it builds a yardage book, the course is mapped in OpenStreetMap. Download that PDF: it's the source for uphill and downhill numbers.
  2. Check the mapping is complete on FairwayMapper. Open fairwaymapper.com, search the course and go hole by hole: a red dot in the hole list usually means a feature is missing. Make sure every hole has a green, a white tee box, a fairway on par 4s and 5s, and trees where they're in play. Trace anything missing in Mapping Tools at the zoom where the existing bunkers sit exactly on the sand in the photo (the imagery shifts between zoom levels), then tap Publish. Allow a few hours for edits to reach the exports below.
  3. Export the map data (easiest on a laptop). Go to overpass-turbo.eu, zoom in on the course, paste the query below, press Run, then Export → GeoJSON → download.
  4. Get the scorecard for your tees. A screenshot of the white-tee scorecard (Hole19 or the club card) showing length, par and stroke index for all 18, plus the course rating and slope.
  5. Review the club's own course guide. Before every new course, check the club website's hole-by-hole pages for three things: the official yardages for each tee, the pro tips or "how to play" notes, and any hole diagrams or course maps. Send Claude the page links and screenshots of the diagrams (the images can't be read from a link).
  6. Send everything to Claude in the Golf project: "Add [course] from these files, white tees."
  7. Claude builds, reconciles and checks it. Official yardages correct any scorecard errors. Club tips become caddy rules (no driver, tee-shot targets, aim lines) and trouble zones (OB, lost-ball trees, hidden hazards), with club distances converted to your tee. Measured elevation always beats generic "take an extra club" advice. Diagrams are compared with the map to fill any missing hazards. Every hole must then pass the quality checks: tee matched to the card, its own fairway only, landing spots on that fairway, green depth plausible, card total matching. Anything that fails is fixed or flagged before you get the file.
  8. Upload the new index.html to Golf-Backpocket as usual.
  9. Verify on your first round. On a few holes, check one number with your rangefinder (a bunker carry or the green front). Set a "my club" override wherever your local knowledge beats the plan, and send any corrections back.
Overpass query
[out:json][timeout:60];
( way["golf"]({{bbox}}); relation["golf"]({{bbox}});
  way["natural"~"wood|water|scrub"]({{bbox}}); node["natural"="tree"]({{bbox}}); );
out geom;
Not mapped? You can draw it yourself with FairwayMapper (free, in the browser), or add the course here with pars only and no maps.

About

Your personal caddy — practice program, round book, scorecard and handicap in one place. Built around your bag, your feels and the Northern Beaches.

Data — stored privately in this browser (localStorage). Nothing is sent anywhere.

Handicap — simplified World Handicap System: best-of-recent differentials. An estimate for tracking, not an official index.

Add to home screen — open in Safari → Share → Add to Home Screen, and always open it from that icon so your log stays in one place.
